title: Carrots
text: Carrots in three minutes. Sweet, crunchy roots, straight from your own garden. Here's how to sow them, look after them, and bring in the harvest.

title:
Start with
good soil
text: Choose a sunny spot with loose, well-drained soil. Remove stones and break up hard lumps. Skip fresh manure, which can encourage forked roots. On heavy or shallow ground, choose a short-rooted variety.
note: Loose soil · fewer stones · no fresh manure

title:
Wait for
warmer soil
text: For a straightforward UK crop, sow from April to June, once the soil is workable and warming. Early varieties can go under cover in March. Sow another small batch every few weeks for a longer harvest.
note: Timing varies with variety and local weather

title:
Sow where
they will grow
text: Water a shallow drill, then scatter seed thinly, about one centimetre deep. Leave fifteen to thirty centimetres between rows. Cover lightly and firm gently. Sow direct: transplanting can damage the developing root.
note: Rows 15–30 cm apart · follow your seed packet

title:
Be patient.
Keep it moist.
text: Germination can take around two to three weeks, longer in cold soil. Keep the seed zone moist, without waterlogging it. Watch for slugs while seedlings are small, and remove weeds before they take over.
note: Moist at seed depth · never waterlogged

title:
Give each
root space
text: Thin only crowded seedlings, leaving five to eight centimetres between plants. Work gently in damp conditions, remove the thinnings, and firm the soil around the plants you keep. Avoid bruising the foliage.
note: Thin gently · remove thinnings · replace mesh

title:
Keep growth
steady
text: Once established, water deeply during prolonged dry spells. Pots need checking more often. A drought followed by a sudden soaking can split roots. Weed carefully by hand close to the carrots, keeping disturbance to a minimum.
note: Steady moisture helps prevent split roots

title:
Keep carrot
fly out
text: Carrot fly larvae tunnel into the roots. Cover the whole crop with fine insect mesh, securing every edge. Replace it straight after weeding or thinning, and avoid ground where carrots were recently grown.
note: Cover the whole crop · secure all edges

title:
Pull them
young & sweet
text: Harvest when the roots are big enough to eat, usually twelve to sixteen weeks after sowing. Baby carrots may be ready around eight weeks. Start at one end of the row; loosen hard soil with a fork before pulling.
note: Size matters more than the calendar

title:
Keep the
harvest coming
text: Enjoy some freshly pulled. For storage, lift before hard frost or prolonged wet weather. Trim the leaves and pack sound roots in sand in a cool, airy place. Check regularly and remove any that rot.
note: Use damaged roots promptly · check stored roots

title:
Sow thinly.
Grow steadily.
Harvest sweet.
text: Good soil, thin sowing, steady moisture, and mesh. That's carrots in three minutes. Follow Hackriculture for more practical ways to grow your own food.
